markdown_report:
At 10% progress, select **a conservative competitive-negative curriculum for the existing prefix/suffix NextItNet objective**. This changes sampling while retaining the starting model and its weak recent-suffix supervision; improvement remains untested.

Three starting-point insights guide the experiment. First, shared prefix/suffix parameters permit one-checkpoint deployment. Cropping nevertheless assumes the retained context supports the same target, so its auxiliary weight should remain weak. Second, near-perfect uniform training-audit hit rates coexist with weaker competitive rankings. Movies’ prefix-lexical hit rate falls from 0.98965 to 0.72450, motivating better discrimination rather than an embedding-collapse intervention. Third, users reject both functionally unsuitable related products and entertainment matches missing specific qualities. Competitive supervision could address these distinct failures, but interaction labels do not establish compatibility or mood.

Three literature insights refine the direction. AHNS and R²NS motivate progressive, stochastic hardness. Their findings support a cautious transfer hypothesis, without establishing NextItNet gains. Correcting the LogQ Correction distinguishes estimation from deliberate sampling bias. An uncorrected competitive objective must therefore be described as such. MARS motivates finer textual distinctions. Its pretrained approach does not validate a scratch-trained encoder under these restrictions.

The framework separates three directions: **candidate discrimination**, **context selection**, and **item representation**. Sampling changes which distinctions receive gradients; cropping changes visible evidence; text changes item features. Keeping these interventions separate makes early experiments interpretable.

Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder. Each assessment gives a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Five assessments |
|---|---|
| Competitive-negative curriculum, selected [AHNS, R²NS] | O 3: +targeted transfer, −established sampling; P 7: +reusable curriculum, −false negatives; U 7: +specific functional/taste competition, −no intent labels; M 8: +direct competitive discrimination, −training-only evidence; D 3: +sampler change, −pool scoring cost |
| Timestamp-conditioned causal tap attenuation [drift-aware subsequences] | O 5: +NextItNet adaptation, −existing context gates; P 7: +context control, −unidentified boundaries; U 7: +stale interests, −compatibility unresolved; M 4: +context hypothesis, −no measured drift failure; D 7: +one network, −causal tap rewrite |
| Joint scratch title encoder [MARS] | O 3: +permitted adaptation, −standard fusion; P 6: +fine distinctions, −sparse supervision; U 8: +function and musical descriptors, −text incompleteness; M 6: +lexical discrimination, −overlap shortcuts; D 6: +small encoder, −tokenization/export cost |

For the selected idea, warm up with uniform candidates, then replace a small fraction with stochastic selections from moderately competitive candidates. Use identical candidates for complete-prefix and weak suffix losses. Retain uniform coverage and avoid deterministic hardest-item selection. This explicitly targets broad functional matches displacing concrete complements and broad entertainment matches missing specific taste; these are hypotheses, not demonstrated user benefits.

Compare against the unchanged starting objective using pinned macro validation HR@10. Preserve all four categories, seeds, budgets, diagnostic interfaces, and one checkpoint/category. Deploy one complete-prefix pass; never use suffix-score fusion. Re-run the frozen competitive audit as supporting evidence, preserving its definitions and unavailable fields.

idea.description: Replace a small fraction of uniform negatives in the starting shared-parameter prefix/suffix NextItNet objective with progressively introduced stochastic competitive negatives. Preserve one jointly trained NextItNet and one selected checkpoint per category, with complete-prefix-only inference.
idea.motivation: The current diagnosis shows strong fitted-training ranking against uniform candidates but weaker ranking against popular and lexical competitors, especially in Movies_and_TV and Industrial_and_Scientific. The proposed sampler targets two explicit user failures: broadly related but functionally unsuitable products displacing concrete matches, and entertainment recommendations matching broad genre or era while missing more specific qualities. Neither improvement nor compatibility reasoning is established by these observations. Current Electronics pairwise errors are only 0.20%; the older 6.38% figure must not guide this experiment.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate into the supplied corrected baseline rather than reconstructing its absent source. Retain its NextItNet backbone, optimizer, sample_batch target alignment, prefix construction, and existing weak suffix coefficient. The experimental change is negative sampling alone; if the host baseline does not yet implement the starting prefix/suffix objective, first establish that objective as the reference rather than combining two unmeasured changes.

A concrete initial configuration is 99 unique negatives per supported target, with five epochs of uniform warm-up. Over the next fifteen epochs, linearly increase the competitive fraction to 0.20. These values are proposed settings, not established optima. Build a separate pool of up to 256 unique eligible training-catalog IDs for each complete prefix, score it through the current network without gradients in evaluation mode, and sample competitive IDs uniformly without replacement from score ranks 9 through 64. Restore the prior training mode afterward. This deliberately avoids always selecting the maximum-scoring item. Eligible IDs exclude padding, the target, and model-visible prefix items; never consult later events or held-out labels for sampling. Excluding seen prefix items can suppress repeat-purchase alternatives, so preserve the baseline's policy if it differs and document the choice before comparison. Fill remaining slots uniformly without replacement, excluding already selected IDs. Reduce the requested count explicitly when the eligible catalog is too small.

Use the same target and candidate IDs for the complete-prefix loss and its suffix auxiliary loss. Keep the full-prefix loss dominant. Optimize uncorrected sampled-candidate cross-entropy; this is a deliberately biased competitive ranking objective, not an unbiased full-softmax estimator. Do not apply a uniform logQ correction to mined candidates. Unobserved candidates may be relevant: stochastic moderate hardness and a small fraction mitigate exposure but do not resolve false negatives. Target-conditioned lexical-oracle audit candidates must remain diagnostic only.

Mining uses the currently trained network, not another predictor, and adds no inference component. Bound pool scoring to the positions already supervised by the supplied training objective and record realized mining GPU time. Keep maximum epochs 200 and exactly 200 batches per epoch, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and a dedicated sampling RNG seeded 42 where supported. Use one GPU per trial. All training, mining, diagnostics, debugging, and failed trials consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; concurrent slots do not expand it. No performance claim is made here, and no execution was performed.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl and their existing routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; all artifacts remain under the trial directory. Select using only the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 and retain the existing validation/checkpoint schedule. Record every validation query. Do not read hidden test files, other trials, or their checkpoints.

Keep ModelView.model as the actual trained nn.Module, along with item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Diagnostics must score the actual trained features, distinguish fitted-training audit ranks from validation HR@10, and retain unavailable validation/reload fields unless genuinely measured. Treat embedding-collapse scores near 0.5 according to their cosine definition. Preserve the twenty-user full-catalog unseen-item diagnostic process; report explicit functional and entertainment rejection reasons separately from uncertain judgments when supported. Only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions are available; do not infer simulator traits or consume the generic unavailable metadata fields.

Inference remains architecturally unchanged: one complete-prefix forward pass, one checkpoint per category, and no independent score additions. Preserve the generated predictor writer and checkpoint architecture/configuration consistency. For left padding, locate the final nonzero position by positional maximum, never count-1; preserve the corrected baseline's explicit empty-history policy. Verify generated-predictor reload score agreement, category routing, candidate mappings, and causal target alignment using permitted inputs. Because no baseline source is included, the pseudocode is an integration specification rather than a fabricated runnable train.py.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_FIXED_CATEGORIES:
    model = supplied_corrected_nextitnet_cold_start(seed=42)
    # One network; sampler uses a dedicated RNG seeded 42.
    for epoch in range(min(configured_epochs, 200)):
        fraction = 0.20 * clamp((epoch - 4) / 15, 0, 1)
        for batch_index in range(200):
            batch = family_specific_sample_batch(...)
            # Enumerate only the baseline's supported, causally aligned targets.
            for prefix, target in supported_training_examples(batch):
                eligible = training_catalog_without_padding_target_and_visible_prefix(
                    prefix, target)
                K = min(99, len(eligible))
                hard_count = min(round(fraction * K), K)
                competitive = []
                if hard_count > 0:
                    pool = sample_unique(eligible, min(256, len(eligible)), sampler_rng)
                    prior_mode = model.training
                    model.eval()
                    with no_grad():
                        h = final_nonpadding_feature(model.log2feats(left_pad(prefix)))
                        pool_scores = model.predict_score(h, pool)
                    model.train(prior_mode)
                    ranked = sort_by_score_then_id(pool, pool_scores)
                    moderate = ranked[8:64]
                    competitive = sample_unique(
                        moderate, min(hard_count, len(moderate)), sampler_rng)
                remaining = eligible.difference(competitive)
                uniform = sample_unique(remaining, K - len(competitive), sampler_rng)
                candidates = [target] + competitive + uniform
                full_scores = score_complete_prefix(model, prefix, candidates)
                full_loss = cross_entropy(full_scores, positive_index=0)
                suffix = existing_starting_idea_suffix(prefix)
                if suffix_has_less_context_than(prefix):
                    suffix_scores = score_suffix_same_network(model, suffix, candidates)
                    suffix_loss = cross_entropy(suffix_scores, positive_index=0)
                    loss = full_loss + existing_weak_suffix_weight * suffix_loss
                else:
                    loss = full_loss
                accumulate_using_baseline_batch_reduction(loss)
            baseline_optimizer_step()
        apply_existing_validation_and_checkpoint_policy()
    export_one_selected_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor(category)

# Deployment: no mining, auxiliary suffix, or score fusion.
features = model.log2feats(sequence)
positions = arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
last = where(sequence.ne(0), positions[None, :], -1).amax(dim=1)
nonempty = last.ge(0)
scores[nonempty] = model.predict_score(
    features[nonempty, last[nonempty]], candidates[nonempty])
# Explicitly apply the supplied baseline policy to empty rows.
# Preserve all diagnostic contracts and measure exported-predictor parity separately.

originality.positive: Provides a focused transfer of progressive stochastic negative sampling to the diagnosed NextItNet objective while preserving single-model deployment.
originality.negative: Adaptive hardness, candidate pools, and stochastic selection have direct precedents; the proposed schedule is an incremental experiment.

future_potential.positive: Could establish whether competitive supervision improves specific ranking distinctions without architectural or inference overhead.
future_potential.negative: False negatives, fitted-target memorization, and mismatch with uniform benchmark candidates may prevent generalization or user-facing gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Changes training candidate construction while retaining the backbone, scoring head, checkpoint format, and deployed forward pass.
code_difficulty.negative: Unique exclusions, causal per-position pools, training-mode restoration, shared candidates, and mining compute require careful integration with the absent baseline source.

related_work.title: AHNS (AAAI 2024)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes adaptive hardness intended to mitigate false-positive and false-negative effects.
Motivates progressive hardness rather than deterministic maximum-score negatives.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this NextItNet benchmark.
Adaptive hardness does not identify truly negative unobserved items.

related_work.title: R²NS (WWW 2026)
contributions: The supplied summary describes uniform warm-up, global candidate recall, and progressively harder stochastic selection for sequential recommendation.
limitations: Reported backbone experiments do not include NextItNet.
The proposed small random candidate pool is a simplified adaptation, not a reproduction.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Distinguishes always-included positive contributions from sampled negatives in sampled-softmax estimation.
limitations: Does not justify applying a uniform-proposal correction after model-dependent mining.
The selected experiment deliberately optimizes an uncorrected competitive objective.

related_work.title: Preference-Drift-Aware Subsequence Learning
contributions: The supplied summary describes learned context boundaries and recent/global context selection.
limitations: Does not establish that arbitrary suffixes preserve next-target supervision.

related_work.title: MARS
contributions: Motivates attribute-specific textual representations and finer user-item matching.
limitations: Its pretrained text approach is outside this experiment's permitted resources.
Does not establish equivalent gains from a scratch-trained lightweight encoder.
